sentences.text: Hello every welcome to the slow English podcast. I'm Emily and today we are traveling to a
magical city in Jordan called Petra. Petra is very old and very beautiful. It is famous for buildings
carved in red rocks. Walking here feels like going back in time. Let's explore this amazing place
together. Part two, where is Petra? Petra is in the south of Jordan. It is in a desert area with
mountains and rocks. The nearest city is Wadi Musa. You can also reach Petra from Amman,
the capital of Jordan in a few hours by car. It is one of the most visited tourist places in Jordan.
Part three, a short history of Petra. Petra was built over 2,000 years ago by the Navatians.
They were skilled people who lived in the desert. The city was an important trade center for spices,
silk, and other goods. Petra was lost for many years and rediscovered in 1812.
Today, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the new seven wonders of the world.
Part four, the Sikh and Treasury. To enter Petra, you walk through a narrow canyon called the Sikh.
It is beautiful, high, and colorful. At the end of the Sikh, you see the famous treasury, Alcazna.
It is carved into the red rocks and looks incredible. Many people take photos here
and admire the detail of the stones. Part five, other monuments in Petra. Petra has many
other monuments and tombs. There is the monastery at there, very big and on top of a hill. You can
climb 800 steps to reach it. From there, you see the desert and mountains, amazing views.
There are also temples, theaters, and houses carved into rocks.
Part six, the people of Petra. Today, the people living near Petra are called Bedouins.
They are very friendly and help tourists. They sell souvenirs like jewelry, scarves, and crafts.
Some also offer camel or horse rides to explore the area. Bedouins are proud of their traditions
and culture. They are happy to share it with visitors.
Part seven, food in Jordan. Jordanian food is delicious. In Petra, you can try Mansaf,
the national dish made with lamb and rice. People also eat falafel, hummus, and fresh bread.
For dessert, trabaklava, sweet, nutty, and delicious.
Tea and coffee are very important in Jordan. Visitors are often offered to drink as a sign of welcome.
Part eight, nature around Petra. Petra is in a desert, but there are mountains and valleys nearby.
You can see colorful rocks, cliffs, and sand. Sometimes, you see small plants and flowers growing
between stones. The desert is calm and quiet, perfect to feel peace and history.
Part nine, festivals and culture. Petra is also a cultural center. At night, there is a special
event called Petra by night. People walk through the sick with candles and see the treasury lit by
lights. It feels magical and unforgettable. The culture of Jordan includes music, dance,
and traditional stories. Part ten, weather in Petra. Petra has a desert climate.
It is hot in summer and cooler in winter. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit.
Bring water, a hat, and comfortable shoes to walk in the desert.
Even in winter, the sun shines bright and makes the red rocks glow. Part 11, daily life in Petra.
Life in Petra is quiet, active with tourists. Bedouin families take care of homes,
sell souvenirs, and guide visitors. Children play and sometimes help their families.
Visitors come to explore, learn, and take photos. The city has a mix of history, culture, and daily life.
Part 12, goodbye from Petra. Thank you for joining me on this trip to Petra, Jordan.
It is a city full of history, culture, and magic. From the sick to the treasury and the monastery,
Petra shows the skill and creativity of the Nabataeans. If you visit Jordan,
Petra is a must-see place. Goodbye, or as people in Jordan say, Ma'a Asalama.
